diagram_classification: cosmological (probably a diagram of the elements and the cosmic quaternities, with a possible computistical/calendrical use)
interpretation: The diagram shows a green square frame enclosing an orange-red rhombus (a square set on its point). Four unfilled, ringed circles sit at its vertices (top, right, bottom, left). Four larger coloured discs sit in the corners of the frame: dark red with a grid in the upper left, pale grey-green in the upper right, dark green in the lower right, and black or dark grey in the lower left. The rhombus links the four vertex nodes in a closed cycle, which suggests a fourfold system. The four vertex circles most plausibly stand for the cardinal points or the four primary divisions of the cosmos, and the four coloured discs for the four elements or qualities, each given a distinct colour. The thin cross inside the rhombus (a vertical line from the top node and a horizontal line across the lower part) marks an axis or a division into quarters. The rhombus inscribed in the square probably expresses the correspondence between the cosmic order and the elements. The picture contains no text, so the exact identification of each element and quarter is uninterpreted and is only a probable reading.
evidence: The structure is four-part throughout: four ringed nodes at the vertices of the rhombus and four coloured discs in the corners of the square frame. The closed orange bands link the nodes in a cycle, and the cross lines mark axes or quarters. The distinct colours (red grid, pale, green, black) point to differentiated categories such as elements or qualities. The diagram has no legible labels, so the specific meanings of the colours, circles and axes cannot be confirmed from the image.
